newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London ended mixed with November and January unchanged at $1,500 and 1,430 per tonne respectively. March added $8 to close at $1,377.

In New York arabica futures firmed with renewed emphasis on the widening of the December/March spread. Expectations of a drawdown in GCA stock figures touched off a late wave of buying by locals, trade sources said.

Green Coffee Association stock figures for October, due after the close of business on Friday, are expected to show a decline of between 200,000 and 300,000 60- kg bags, although some predict the drawdown could be as large as 500,000 bags. In September stocks fell to 1.611 million bags, their lowest level since the GCA began tracking inventories eight years ago.

COLOMBIA - The USDA Attache lowered its Colombian coffee crop estimate for 1995/96 (October/September) by 500,000 bags to 12 million bags while the 1996/97 estimate was also lowered by the same amount to 12.5 million bags, due to unfavourable weather. These figures are at odds with recent official Colombian estimates of between 10.5 to 11.0 million bags in 1996/97 down from 12.9 million bags produced in 1995/96.

IVORY COAST - According to official sources coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) could reach 3.8 million bags or even more which compares to an estimated 2.8 million bags in 1995/96 in spite of a reduction in the farm- gate guide price for coffee by over 28 per cent to 500 CFA francs per kilo. It was said that the coffee sector is beginning to reap the benefits of investment from a special fund which has improved the state of plantations, making them more productive and efficient.

BRAZIL - Brazilians are drinking more coffee every day and the country should become a top consumer within about ten years, Carlos Melles, a Brazilian congressman representing Minas Gerais said. He added domestic coffee consumption had risen 1.0 million 60-kg bags last year to a total of 11 million bags and Brazilians were expected to consume 12 million bags in 1996. By the year 2000, consumption was seen totalling 15 million bags and the country looked certain to surpass the United States and become the world's top coffee consumer within 10 to 12 years.

IRELAND - Ireland imported 56,100 bags of coffee in January/June 1996, 4 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 15 per cent to 114,900 bags. The country gets most of its coffee in the form of solubles from the U.K.
